newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs endorse moves to stamp out EU budget fraud.
newsitem.headline: MEPs endorse moves to stamp out EU budget fraud.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Thursday measures designed to protect the European Union's financial interests and combat fraud.

MEPs adopted without amendments a draft regulation -- COM(95)690 -- which will give the European Commission's fraud prevention unit (UCLAF) greater powers to carry out on-the-spot checks in the member states, to ensure EU money is being properly used.
The member states administer 80 percent of the EU budget.

Parliament also approved, with amendments, a proposal made by the Commission on January 19 to annex a second protocol to the Convention on the Protection of the European Communities' Financial Interests.
Among other things, the convention defines fraud, sets out penal sanctions and contains provisions for extradition, prosecution, cooperation and the settlement of disputes about its interpretation.
The proposed second protocol helps to complete the legal framework by making it possible to regulate areas such as jurisdiction and judicial cooperation.
